posts.title: Single-leg training vs squats: 2026 evidence for home gyms
posts.excerpt: A July 2026 review of 24 randomized trials found single-leg work favored one-leg strength and jumping, while two-legged work favored bilateral strength, per Mind Muscle Perfection. It found no clear…
posts.body: A July 2026 review of 24 randomized trials found single-leg work favored one-leg strength and jumping, while two-legged work favored bilateral strength, per [Mind Muscle Perfection](https://mindmuscleperfection.com/single-leg-training-vs-squats-2026-home-gym-guide/). It found no clear muscle-growth advantage for either approach, so the practical takeaway is specificity: train the movement you want to get stronger at.

posts.body: On October 22, Justice Department lawyers asked Ninth Circuit judges in Pasadena to dissolve the Perez-Funez injunction that requires agents to advise unaccompanied children of their rights before accepting voluntary departure, in argument [detailed by Immigration Analytics](https://immigration-analytics.com/2026/10/23/perez-funez-injunction-ninth-circuit/) from Courthouse News' October 22 reporting ("Feds ask Ninth Circuit to scrap 40-year-old safeguards for unaccompanied minor migrants"). The panel of Judges Patrick Bumatay, Lawrence VanDyke, and Salvador Mendoza Jr. did not signal how it would rule.

posts.title: Extra carbs built no extra muscle in trained men
posts.excerpt: Twenty trained men spent eight weeks on each supplement, with the carb version adding about 485 kcal a day. Muscle size, lean mass, squat and knee-extension strength showed no significant differences…
posts.body: Twenty trained men [spent eight weeks on each supplement](https://macrosmeasure.com/blog/do-you-need-carbs-to-build-muscle-what-the-2026-crossover-trial-found-in-trained-men), with the carb version adding about 485 kcal a day. Muscle size, lean mass, squat and knee-extension strength showed no significant differences between 30g protein plus ~54g carbs and 30g protein plus 4g carbs.

posts.title: ORR says 1-year-old was never in immigration court alone; blames Acacia for filing gap
posts.excerpt: ORR's timeline says the 1-year-old was never in immigration court alone: he and his 17-year-old mother were encountered near Naco, Arizona, on June 25, and she accompanied him to every proceeding.…
posts.body: ORR's [timeline](https://foxnews.com/politics/fed-timeline-challenges-reports-migrant-baby-facing-immigration-judge-alone) says the 1-year-old was never in immigration court alone: he and his 17-year-old mother were encountered near Naco, Arizona, on June 25, and she accompanied him to every proceeding. The agency pins the July 8 gap on contractor Acacia, which completed legal orientation on July 1 but never filed the E28 notice of appearance.
